label: Community bank / credit union
description: A US community financial institution (about $100 M to $10 B in assets) that runs its own branches and outsources core processing: a community bank or thrift under the OCC, Fed or FDIC, or a federally insured credit union under the NCUA, plus the state regulator. The core and digital banking platforms, wires through FedLine, ACH, FedNow, card processing and the ATM fleet; branch alarms, vaults and cameras under the Bank Protection Act; and the 36-hour / 72-hour regulator notices, SAR, Reg E and GLBA clocks that go with them.

vocabulary.facility: the institution (branches and drive-ups, the ATM fleet, the operations center and the core and digital banking platforms)
vocabulary.public: customers and members, business clients and the community
vocabulary.frontline: tellers, branch managers, contact-center agents, wire-room staff, fraud analysts, deposit-operations staff
vocabulary.operationsCenter: the operations center and the incident management team's conference room

it: core banking platform (Fiserv, Jack Henry, FIS; Symitar, KeyStone or XP2 at credit unions)
teller / branch platform with offline 'store and forward' mode
online and mobile banking, bill pay, P2P and remote deposit capture (Q2, Alkami, Banno)
cash management / business online banking: ACH origination, wires, positive pay, dual control
wire transfer system: Fedwire Funds via FedLine Advantage or FedLine Direct
FedACH origination and receipt; FedNow and RTP instant payments
card processing and EFT network (debit authorization, card management, fraud scoring)
ATM / ITM fleet switching and remote monitoring
item processing and check image exchange
BSA/AML and fraud monitoring, CTR / SAR case management and OFAC screening (Verafin, Abrigo)
email (Microsoft 365), Active Directory, VPN, EDR and SIEM / MSSP
DDoS mitigation / CDN for the website and online banking
ot: branch intrusion alarm and holdup / panic alarm panel monitored by a central station
CCTV / VMS in the lobby, teller line, drive-up, ATM vestibule and vault
vaults, time locks, dual-control combinations and the night depository
ATM safes and cassettes, vestibule card-access doors and anti-skimming devices
PACS at the operations center and data center
data center UPS, generator, HVAC and fire suppression

roles.name: Chief Operating Officer (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Runs the incident management team, activates the BCP, picks manual workarounds (offline teller, stand-in processing) and sets the order of business-line recovery.

roles.name: Bank Security Officer
roles.description: Owns robbery response, alarms and CCTV, the vault and night drop, ATM physical attacks, and the liaison with local police and the FBI.

roles.name: Information Security Officer / CISO (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Runs the investigation with the CIO, engages the IR retainer firm and the insurer's breach coach, and decides with Legal whether the event is a notification incident.

roles.name: Marketing & Communications Director (PIO)
roles.description: Owns press holding statements, social media, the website banner, lobby signage and employee messaging.

roles.name: President & Chief Executive Officer
roles.description: Declares a crisis, approves regulator and board notices, and makes the ransom-payment and branch-closure calls.

roles.name: BSA/AML Officer
roles.description: Owns the SAR decision and timing, FinCEN advisory keywords, OFAC screening and law-enforcement hold requests.

roles.name: Fraud & Payments Operations Manager
roles.description: Owns wire recalls and callback verification, ACH returns, card blocks, account freezes and the Reg E error-resolution clock.

roles.name: Chief Risk Officer / Compliance Officer
roles.description: Owns the regulator notice (36 h / 72 h), the state regulator notice, the GLBA customer-notice decision and the decision log.

outsideParties: the primary federal regulator: the OCC, the Federal Reserve Bank, the FDIC regional office or the NCUA regional office
the state banking or credit union regulator
FinCEN and OFAC; Treasury OCCIP (the sector risk management agency)
Federal Reserve Financial Services (Fedwire, FedACH, FedNow and FedLine support)
the FBI field office and IC3, the U.S. Secret Service Cyber Fraud Task Force and local police
the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (mail-theft check fraud)
CISA and the state attorney general
the core processor, digital banking vendor, card processor and EFT network
the ATM servicer and armored carrier
the correspondent bank or corporate credit union
FS-ISAC and the state bankers or credit union league
the MSSP, IR retainer firm, cyber insurer and breach coach, and the DDoS mitigation provider
business customers with payroll files in flight and municipal depositors
mediaChannels: Facebook community groups and Nextdoor ('is the bank down?')
X and Reddit posts with screenshots of the online-banking error page
the local TV assignment desk and the local business journal
a ransomware leak-site listing naming the institution or its vendor
the institution's own website banner, app push notifications and IVR greeting

sceneAnchors.public: inside a community bank branch lobby on a weekday morning: customers in line at a wood teller counter with three tellers, a branch manager's glass office, rope stanchions, a rack of brochures, warm light
sceneAnchors.control: inside a bank operations center: staff at desks with headsets and dual monitors, a printed wire-room checklist taped to a cubicle wall, a locked cabinet of FedLine tokens, fluorescent light
sceneAnchors.exterior: a suburban community bank branch: a brick building with a drive-up canopy and two lanes, a walk-up ATM by the entrance, a small parking lot with a few cars, a flag on a pole, overcast daylight

noiseExamples: a teller drawer out of balance by $20
a customer upset about an overdraft fee
a printer driver failure at the loan desk
pressureExamples: 'is my money safe?' posts with an error-page screenshot
a reporter asking whether the bank paid a ransom
a municipal treasurer demanding confirmation that public funds are secure
a business customer threatening to move payroll
the board chair demanding hourly updates
the state regulator calling before the institution has notified anyone
